findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee was observed to wash their hands and use their bare hand to turn off the faucet, recontaminating the hands. They then proceeded to handle plates of RTE foods while touching the food contact side of the plate. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to ensure that proper hand washing is taking place in the facility at al times.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-801.11: (D) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact READY-TO-EAT FOOD as specified under  3-301.11(B) and (E). 

A dixie cup is observed stored in the Italian beef on the steam table. The PIC was shown and removed the cup to correct the immediate concern. A similar violation was noted on the previous routine inspection at the salad station, making this a repeat situation. Use appropriate utensils while handling RTE foods to prevent bare hand contact of the foods.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple nozzles of the fountain drink machines are observed soiled during this inspection. To a lesser extent the soda gun in the bar area was also soiled. The PIC indicated that they were cleaned a couple times a week. This seems to be insufficient for the facility’s current use. The nozzles were removed and cleaned during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that they are cleaned often enough to be maintained in a clean state.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C).

Two large tubs of ground beef in the walk in cooler are without date marking. The PIC indicated that they were made yesterday and the day before. Stickers were added to the tubs to correct the violation. Ensure that all RTE TCS foods are labeled with the date that they have their package opened or are cooked.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. 

Two syrup bottles in the standing cooler to the right of the pizza prep station are observed with mold growth on the outside of the containers. The PIC was shown and the items discarded during this inspection to correct. Ensure that the containers for RTE items are maintained clean at all times.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. 

Multiple moist rags in the kitchen are observed on the counters. The PIC was consulted and instructed to maintain the in-use rags in sanitizer solution between uses. The rags were moved during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

On arrival, there was not a sani bucket prepared in the kitchen area. Food handling and preparation activities were observed throughout the kitchen. When discussed with the PIC a bucket was produced to correct the violation. Ensure that there is an in-use sanitizer available at all times that food handling/preparation is taking place.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Allergen training is only available for 3 of the CFPMs during this inspection. Per previous notes the facility has information about taking/retaking the certification. Ensure that all CFPMs have completed allergen training prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.112: Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the PREMISES at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests. 

Observed a number of dead cockroaches under the dish machine on the floor and sticky glue traps. One dead roach was noted under the steam table well along the main prep line. Several dead roaches were noticed in the soda room (on the sticky pads). Continue to work with Bacon’s Pest Control to eliminate the roach infestation. Bacon’s was actively coming every week to two weeks at the beginning of the issue and during baiting. Pest control is now coming back 1x monthly as per usual maintenance. Continue to have staff monitor in the above mentioned areas, as well as under the pizza prep table. Main issues are in the dish machine area. Change sticky pads as needed to remove dead pests. Inspector will follow-up at the next routine inspection (beginning of 2024).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Observed several live roaches at the dish machine area. Noodle steam table was free of roaches. Several were noted on the sticky pad under the pizza prep cooler. None were noted in the soda room. See General Comments for more details. Follow-up on 11/15/2023.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Roach infestation was assessed today. Mitigation efforts were conducted by the facility. Bacon’s Pest Control came last week per PIC and is coming every week until the situation is rectified. Sticky pads are being placed against walls and in corners by the staff. Frequent changes are occurring as roaches are caught. The sticky pads noted today had far less roaches and Inspector did not witness active roaches outside the sticky pads. Roaches are adult size. Inspector did not witness any juvenile roaches. Problem areas noted during the routine inspection: dish machine room, under pizza prep table, under and within the noodle steam table in center of kitchen, soda machine room. Inspector investigated bar more throughly today and did not note any activity. Facility has done major cleaning within the dish room area (power washed floors and coving). No building repairs have been conducted. The dish machine itself was cleaned (still needs more cleaning). Pizza prep table did not have significant debris under the cooler. Steam table has been cleaned underneath and sticky trap placed within the base unit. Soda room has not been cleaned from what is observed. Bacon’s has sprayed within the walls per PIC. Bacon’s noted better control of the infestation as well.

Dish Room: Walls need scrubbed of food debris and mold, re-caulk the dish machine, 3 compartment sink, and hand sink in this area (moldy, coming away), top and underside of the dish machine needs further cleaning (food debris build-up), coving around the perimeter of the dish room is coming away (roaches were coming from behind coving) and needs to be repaired/caulked, all holes in the walls in this area need caulked.
Steam Table: maintain cleanliness under the steam table and change sticky traps as needed.
Soda Room: clean the flooring, put sticky traps around the perimeter.
Pizza Prep Table: maintain nightly cleaning by pulling the cooler away and cleaning/mopping behind this cooler, replace sticky traps around perimeter, clean food splash from walls. Clean the dough prep areas in this area - roaches are attached to the flour dust - maintain cleaning of the dough prep area nightly.

Common house flies were not present during the inspection. Multiple sticky tapes have been changed out for new ones (non-food contact areas).

Inspector will follow-up on 10/26 at 3 pm for further roach infestation assessment. See photo page attached in CDP.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-801.11: (D) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact READY-TO-EAT FOOD as specified under  3-301.11(B) and (E). 

Observed multiple dressing to go containers being used as scoops for the salad toppings and dressings. Cease practice. Scoops need handles because salad is a ready-to-eat food and hands are touching to go cups that are immersed in food. The facility has a sign that states this above the salad prep cooler. Ensure staff is aware of appropriate practices. Discussed with PIC. Inspector discarded to go cups. COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Observed the main kitchen hand sink to have ice dumped within in when Inspector went to wash her hands. Cease practice. Hand sinks are for hand washing only. No dumping of food items should occur in hand sink. Ensure kitchen staff is aware. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. 

Observed the bar hand sink to have no soap in the dispenser. Discussed with PIC. PIC put soap in the dispenser. Ensure staff is aware to replace soap as needed when it runs outs. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the large kitchen vent and ceiling tiles directly above the cook line/steam table line to have a thick layer of dust. This is directly above food-contact areas. Clean the ceiling. Inspector will follow-up on 10/13/23.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.comment:
3-403.11: (A) TCS FOOD cooked, cooled, and reheated shall be reheated to 165F for 15 seconds. (P) (B) If reheated with microwave, FOOD rotated, stirred, covered, and allowed to stand for 2 minutes covered. (P) (C) Commercially processed FOOD shall be reheated to 135F. (P) (D) Reheating may not exceed 2 hours.(P) (E) Unsliced portions of MEAT roasts may be reheated according to oven parameters and minimum TCS conditions. (C)  

Observed the hot holding steam table to have all food at barely above cold holding temperatures (65F) or roughly ~100F for some items. Food appears to be being heated directly in the steam table. Cease practice. Inspector questioned the employee making food in this area and he stated the food was directly put into the steam table. And reheated food needs to be cooked at 165F on the cook line, then brought to the steam table where it remains 135F or above. Discussed with employee and PIC. Inspector asked the employee to reheat all items on the stove top. COS.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

Observed all hot holding items on the steam table to be under 135F. The food is being heated on the steam table itself instead of being heated on the stove top, then transferred to the steam table for hot holding at 135F or above. Discussed with employee who was working in this area. Ensure more active managerial control for staff. Cooking, cooling, and reheating practices (see above violation as well) may cause significant food borne illness if done improperly. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.112: Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the PREMISES at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests. 

Observed multiple full fly strips throughout the facility (away from food-contact areas). Discussed with PIC. Ensure the fly strips are changed out as needed when full. Replace. COS.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Observed roach infestation at the facility. All stages of roach life cycle were present: babies, juveniles, and adults. Inspector noted activity by babies and juveniles. Significant areas of issue were in the dish room, under the noodle steam table at the prep line, under pizza prep cooler (minor), and in the soda line room next to the bar (babies noted). Bacon’s Pest Control has been notified of the issue and has been to the facility twice in the last 3 weeks. Inspector asked PIC to have Bacon’s come weekly to the facility until the issue is resolved. Per PIC, Bacon’s has sprayed, left powder, and put down sticky traps. The facility should purchase their own sticky traps and replace every few days as needed around the perimeters of the hot spot areas listed above. 
Dish Room: Walls need scrubbed of food debris and mold, re-caulk the dish machine, 3 compartment sink, and hand sink in this area (moldy, coming away), top and underside of the dish machine needs a good cleaning (food debris build-up), coving around the perimeter of the dish room is coming away (roaches were coming from behind coving) and needs to be repaired/caulked, all holes in the walls in this area need caulked.
Steam Table: pull the equipment away and clean, replace the sticky traps. Discuss with Bacon’s the most appropriate way to remove the roaches from the machine (open the doors, babies and juveniles are underneath inside). 
Soda Room: clean the flooring, put sticky traps around the perimeter.
Pizza Prep Table: maintain nightly cleaning by pulling the cooler away and cleaning/mopping behind this cooler, replace sticky traps around perimeter, clean food splash from walls. Clean the dough prep areas in this area - roaches are attached to the flour dust.

Common house flies are also present throughout the kitchen. There are multiple fly strips away from food-contact areas but they need replaced. Maintain multiple areas with fly strips, keep drive thru window and back exterior door shut as often as possible. Inspector will follow-up about fly strips on 10/13/23.

Inspector will allow the facility to work with Bacon’s for a plan to eradicate the roaches. Inspector will follow-up on 10/13/23 regarding progress of the above instructions in the areas noted. Discussed pest issues with PIC. See attached photo page in CDP.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the following non-food contact areas in need of cleaning:
1. The large metal shelving unit next to the dish machine (holds dirty dishes) has a layer of food debris and grease on it. Entire shelving unit needs power washed.
2. Cart next to the 3 compartment sink needs power washed (covered in dust).
3. All upper shelving ledges with empty pizza boxes have dusty grates. Clean of dust.
4. Multiple fans on the floors throughout the kitchen have a layer of dust (blowing across kitchen).
5. Flooring underneath the shelving of the walk-in cooler is in need of cleaning (sweep, mop). Walls have food splash as well.
6. Fryer area of the prep line has significant grease build-up behind the fryers on the walls and above the fryers on the walls. Grease is also heavily present on the sides of the equipment.
7. Pizza oven has significant debris on top of the oven. Clean.
8. Walk-in freezer fan has layer of dust.

#1-5 are repeat violations since the last routine inspection on 2/24/23. Discussed with PIC. Ensure routine cleaning of the above mentioned areas. Discuss with staff. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

(REPEAT) Observed the majority of CFPM’s to lack allergen training. It has been completed by one CFPM. Facility has educational paperwork on how to re-take/complete allergen training. Ensure all CFPM’s complete training and print copies of certifications for the public health binder. Discussed with PIC. Correct by next routine inspection. This a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 2/24/23.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.14: A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES. 

Observed almost every hand sink in the facility to lack hand washing signs (all kitchen, bar, employee bathroom, and the women’s bathroom). Provided 5 hand washing signs. Ensure all hand washing stations have a sign that notifies employees to wash hands before returning to food service. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the dish machine to have 0 ppm after multiple runs of the machine. MJ Kellner technician was called during the inspection. One of the piping mechanisms was no longer functioning. Technician corrected the issue. Re-tested: 200 ppm. COS. Ensure staff is aware to frequently check the sanitization concentration of the dish machine. Facility has test strips for bleach above the dish machine. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the following food-contact surfaces to be dirty:
1. Panini maker along the prep line has layer of dust and food debris on the outside of the unit. Unit is in need of cleaning.
2. Interior of multiple bottom prep coolers have food splash from sauces and food debris. 
3. Multiple reach-in coolers have dusty interior ceiling fans.
4. Interior of microwave above the pizza prep area is soiled (was not cleaned before closing last night). PIC cleaned it during the inspection - COS.
5. Reach-in cooler next to ice machine has food debris on the grates.

Discussed routine cleaning of the above areas. Ensure staff is aware to regularly clean out the coolers of food splash and debris, check microwaves for food splash and build-up, and dust the interior fans of reach-in coolers. Wash, rinse, sanitize the above areas. Inspector will follow-up on 3/6/23.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed multiple coolers (reach-in and prep) to lack thermometers. Discussed with PIC. Ensure all cold holding units have thermometers within the units. Ensure facility has extra thermometers on hand to replace as needed. PIC will bring more from the other facility location. Replace by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

Observed multiple seals of reach-in coolers to have damaged gaskets/seals. Discussed with PIC and pointed out each gasket at 3-4 coolers. PIC made a note to order 4 gaskets to replace. Ensure repairs are conducted before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following non-food contact areas in need of cleaning:
1. The large metal shelving unit next to the dish machine (holds dirty dishes) has a layer of food debris and grease on it. Entire shelving unit needs power washed.
2. Cart next to 3 compartment sink needs power washed (covered in dust).
3. All upper shelving ledges with empty pizza boxes have dusty grates. All shelving units with pizza boxes need cleaned of dust.
4. Food splash on the walls near the pizza prep area and the prep sink next to the large standing mixer. 
5. Baffles of the hood system are soiled with grease. Last cleaning with Robert Meacham per the sticker on hood was 7/12/22. Hood is in need of a professional cleaning.
6. Fan on the floor within kitchen is blowing cold air. Fan is heavily coated in dust.
7. Fan of walk-in cooler has a layer of dust and debris.
8. Flooring underneath the shelving of the walk-in cooler is in need of cleaned (sweep, mop).
9. Small fan at the bar area (near hand sink) in need of cleaning. Blowing cold air.
10. Dish machine area wall has black mold. Underneath of dish machine has mold on the walls. 

Discussed above areas with PIC. Ensure routine cleaning of non-food contact surfaces. Have the hood system professionally cleaned soon. Ensure all areas are cleaned by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas in need of physical facility repairs:
1. Hand sink next to 3 compartment sink and the 3 compartment sink itself needs re-caulked: moldy caulk. Replace the caulking.
2. Dish machine area in need of re-caulking: wall connecting dish machine, base coving under the dish machine. Area has black, moldy caulk.
3. Bar hand sink needs caulked to the wall, gap is present between wall and sink.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

Observed multiple mops to be sitting within mop bucket and/or with the wet mop head on the floor. Discussed with PIC. Ensure mops are hung in a manner that allows to air and/or drip dry. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed the only allergen training certifications in the public health folder to be expired. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that all certified food protection manager’s complete the allergen training certification. License is valid for 3 years. Certifications present had just expired in January. Only two were present. Facility has 6 CFPM’s. Provided educational hand out so all CFPM’s can take/re-take the allergen training certification. Keep copies in the public health folder. Ensure license is completed and copies in the folder by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

Multiple cans in the dry storage area are observed with significant dents in the sides. PIC indicated that the cans of mushrooms were a mistake on an order and are not used at the facility. The second item is a can of jalapeño peppers that has a dent in the side significant enough to change how the bottom of the can sits on the shelf. The third is a can of green olives with a wide dent that includes the side seam of the can. Procedures for dented cans and what inspectors are concerned with were reviewed with the PIC. The mushrooms were discarded and the other two cans set aside for credit.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-304.11: (A) FOOD shall only contact surfaces of EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned. (B) SINGLE-SERVICE/USE ARTICLES (C) LINENS.

The soda gun in the bar area is observed with heavy mold growth on the parts usually hidden by the cap/nozzle both on the sprayer and on the inner surface of the nozzle. The item is observed in a pitcher of water and is assumed that it was stored there over night or in an attempt to clean prior to opening. The items should have been cleaned prior to the point that they were as heavily soiled as they appear to be now. The items were cleaned during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. 

Clean food contact utensils are observed stored in locations where they are observed contacting unclean surfaces in: 1) a flat square pan in the server prep line has a sharpie mixed in with spoons intended for soups; 2) a cup on the cook/prep line has spoons used for storing sauces mixed in with a sharpie and date marking stickers/paper. Spoons and containers were moved to dish for cleaning and the sharpies will be stored separately moving foreword.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
(REPEAT SITUATION) 4-903.11: (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. 

In the drive through area, the single service spoons and forks intended for consumer use are stored in trays in the cupboard to the right. The bottom of the trays are observed with dust/ other debris. Multiple spoons were also observed directly soiled. Single service items are not packaged and need to be protected until service. Inspector discussed with the PIC and they said that they would start using cups to store the spoons with the seating surfaces down. The current batch of single service items were discarded during the inspection and the trays cleaned out for use with crackers/ salt and pepper packets.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
(REPEAT SITUATION) 4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The nozzles of the north fountain drink machines are observed with slime build up. PIC is instructed to clean often enough to ensure the items are free of accumulated slime. The nozzles were all cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. 

In the drive through area, the single service spoons and forks intended for consumer use are stored in trays in the cupboard to the right. The bottom of the trays are observed with dust/ other debris. Single service items are not packaged and need to be protected until service. The containers were cleaned and the utensils replaced to correct.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

1) Multiple shelves in the walk in cooler are observed heavily soiled. PIC is instructed to clean often enough to maintain clean. 2) (REPEAT) Shelves in the walk in cooler and the upright cooler next to the pizza station are observed soiled. PIC is instructed to clean often enough to prevent build up.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

The ice bin for the north fountain drink machine as well as the ice bin at the north end of the bar are visibly soiled with food debris and a fly. PIC instructed to clean and maintain clean for the ice stored in the containers. Bins were cleaned during the inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) The nozzles for the soda gun on the north end of the bar is observed with slime build up. 2) The nozzles of the fountain drink machines are observed with slime build up. PIC is instructed to clean often enough to ensure the items are free of accumulated slime. The nozzles were all cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

1) Shelves in the walk in cooler and the upright cooler next to the pizza station are observed soiled. PIC is instructed to clean often enough to prevent build up. 2) All four microwaves observed in the kitchen have some level of soil accumulation. As inspection is taking place at the beginning of the set up for the day, soiled surfaces are believed to be from the previous night. PIC stated that they would be cleaned prior to the end of the inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria. 

On arrival, the sani bucket on the prep line is observed at a concentration estimated to be 50 ppm quat. Quat based sanitizers should be at a minimum of 200 ppm. The bucket was remade to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple nozzles on the fountain drink machine are observed soiled with bacterial slime. Education took place and the nozzles were cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. 

1) On arrival, the sani bucket on the prep line had approximately 1 inch of sanitizer in the bottom and was filled to the top with rags. Rags should be submerged between use. The bucket was changed and sani solution filled to the level of the top of the rags. Violation corrected. 2) Multiple rags around the kitchen area are observed moist and being stored on counters. Discussed with PIC and they will re-educate staff to ensure compliance.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

Utensils are stored in a the dry storage area in a tub with soiled with food debris in the bottom. Utensils and tub were moved to dish for cleaning to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

1) The back wall of the walk in cooler has a dark green colored substance (believed to be mold) that has accumulated in multiple locations. Food is not judged to be in danger of contamination so it is only a cleaning issue. 2) The floor under the shelves in the walk in cooler are observed with an accumulation of food debris. PIC is instructed to clean the walls and floors often enough to prevent an accumulation of soilage.
